shortDescription: China's long-dated bond yields dropped to the lowest in 15 months on Thursday as persistent central bank cash injections pushed down borrowing costs, with traders awaiting a key financial forum next week for clues on the monetary policy path.($1 = 6.6920 Chinese yuan renminbi)

children: China's long-dated bond yields dropped to the lowest in 15 months on Thursday as persistent central bank cash injections pushed down borrowing costs, with traders awaiting a key financial forum next week for clues on the monetary policy path.

China's interbank market stayed flush this week, with the average rate of overnight repos (CN1DRP=CFXS) near a five-month low of around 1.25%, broadly in line with the reported borrowing cost of the central bank's overnight reverse repo operations.

The abundant liquidity has helped push long-dated yields lower. The 10-year government bond yield (CN10YT=RR) dropped to 1.64%, its lowest since July 2025, while the 30-year yield (CN30YT=RR) fell to 2.05%. Prices rise when yields fall.

Despite the absence of any maturing reverse repos since Tuesday, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) kept injecting liquidity via the daily seven-day operations. Separately, its outright reverse repo operations delivered a net 400 billion yuan ($59.77 billion) cash injection this month through three- and six-month tenors.

The market has started to price in monetary easing ahead of the Financial Street Forum next week, analysts at Industrial Securities said. They said expectations were divided: some see scope for cuts to reserve requirements and interest rates, while others bet the central bank could deliver a de facto rate cut by shifting its policy anchor to the overnight reverse repo rate.
The seven-day reverse repo rate is currently the main policy rate, at 1.4%.

The Financial Street Forum will run from October 19 to 22 in Beijing, where regulators are set to unveil reform policies. PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng has used past forums to announce framework changes. In 2025, the PBOC announced the resumption of open market government bond trading during the forum.
